description: Provenance for the public chess engines used only as local benchmark opponents. The binaries themselves live untracked under tests/external_engines/ (see .gitignore). None of this code is read by, copied into, or shipped with agent.py; the engines are run as separate processes behind tests/uci_adapter.py and never enter production.
rules_position: https://aichessathon.com/docs/rules.md forbids third-party engines *in a submission*: 'third party engines are prohibited ... Your moves come from code you wrote', and 'Verification' concerns what is uploaded. Running a public engine locally as a sparring opponent ships nothing and is not covered by that ban. GPL and AGPL obligations attach to distribution; these binaries are executed locally and are neither redistributed nor committed.
acquisition: Each binary is a release asset published by the project's own official repository. No third-party mirror or aggregator was used. Release tags were additionally dereferenced through the forge API and matched against the commit pins already recorded in tests/tournament/engines.lock.json.
build_note: No C++ or Rust toolchain is installed on this machine (cargo, rustc, g++, gcc, clang++, cl, cmake and make are all absent), so the engines were not compiled from source here. The official prebuilt release binaries were used instead, and the compiler and build command are therefore the project's own release build, not one performed locally. This is recorded rather than glossed: we did not reproduce these builds.

engines.version_caveat: The leaderboard says 'Rustic Alpha 3' without a patch level. The official download publishes Alpha 3.0.6. This local engine is therefore NOT established to be byte-identical to the leaderboard entry, only the same Alpha 3 series. No claim of identity is made.

engines.commit_verified_against: GitHub annotated tag dereference, and tests/tournament/engines.lock.json
engines.defect: This Windows binary answers exactly one `go` per process and then closes stdout; the adapter observes EOF on the second search and reports a crash. Reproduced three times with plain sequencing and with an `isready` resynchronisation between searches. Sending `ucinewgame` before every `go` does keep the process alive, but that clears the engine's transposition table on every move, which would make it materially weaker than the leaderboard entry and would make the match unequal. It is therefore excluded rather than crippled.

stockfish.reason: Stockfish is an analysis oracle, not a comparable competition target, and nothing in this experiment required an external oracle: every rated correction was established with our own engine at a fixed depth, which keeps the evidence chain inside our own source.
